## Victor Vran (2015, Haemimont Games)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Vran
- https://bigbossbattle.com/on-victor-vran-arpg/
- https://game-wisdom.com/analysis/victor-vran
- https://store.steampowered.com/app/345180/Victor_Vran_ARPG/

**Key facts:**
- Released July 24, 2015 for PC/Mac/Linux by Bulgarian studio Haemimont Games.
- Classless: build identity from two weapon slots (each with 3 skills = 4 specials simultaneously), Destiny Cards (passive buffs that replace class framework), Demon Powers (overcharge ultimates via combo fill).
- Hex system: player-equippable negative passive modifiers that increase difficulty in exchange for improved gold and drop rates — entirely optional.
- Overkill mechanic: defeating enemies with excess damage reduces cooldowns, rewarding precise burst timing.
- Dodge roll present but NO invincibility frames; avoidance requires spatial positioning.
- Endgame: 5 optional challenges per district (varied objectives), Hex stacking.
- Transmutation: combine same-rarity items to reroll/add properties.
- Co-op: 2-player online or local.
- DLCs: Motorhead: Through the Ages (licensed music stages), Fractured Worlds (challenge endgame).
- Overkill Edition (2017) bundles all content.
- Metacritic: 75 PC, 77 Xbox One.
- Weakness: narrow loot pool, life-steal weapon dominance, shallow build diversity vs. D3/PoE.

## Wolcen Lords of Mayhem (2020, Wolcen Studio)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://wolcen.fandom.com/wiki/Gate_of_Fates
- https://store.steampowered.com/app/424370/Wolcen_Lords_of_Mayhem/
- https://www.toolify.ai/ai-news/wolcen-lords-of-mayhem-review-action-rpg-impressions-analysis-3827100
- https://requnix.com/wolcen-lords-of-mayhem-review/

**Key facts:**
- Released February 2020 (5 years Early Access). Developer: Wolcen Studio (France). Engine: CryEngine.
- Classless. Skills drop as loot with Affinity alignment (Ferocity/Toughness/Wisdom) and are modified via attached modifiers.
- Gate of Fates passive tree: three concentric rings (3 inner / 6 middle / 12 outer segments). Player can ROTATE each ring independently, physically changing which segment connections are accessible. Unique in genre.
- Nodes group into archetype clusters: Warmonger, Soldier of Misfortune, Plaguebringer, etc.
- Combat: fast, flashy, dodge-roll-centric with Break Bar on tougher enemies.
- Stormfall: account-wide city hub built with Primordial Affinity currency from endgame runs. Buildings unlock services, passive bonuses, and mission types. Not per-character.
- Endgame: skill duplication unlock (run same skill with different modifier sets).
- Launch problems: server outages, balance bugs, poor reception at 1.0. Post-launch patches improved significantly.
- Co-op: up to 4 players online.
- Unique drop behavior: rare items shift entire builds.

## Minecraft Dungeons (2020, Mojang Studios / Double Eleven)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://xboxera.com/2020/05/27/review-minecraft-dungeons/
- https://mattbrett.com/blog/reviews/minecraft-dungeons/
- https://explosionnetwork.com/minecraft-dungeons-review/

**Key facts:**
- Released May 26, 2020. Developers: Mojang Studios + Double Eleven. Publisher: Xbox Game Studios. Engine: Unreal Engine 4.
- Target audience: family/mixed-age co-op. Deliberately maximally accessible ARPG.
- Loadout: melee weapon + ranged weapon + up to 3 artifact slots. No classes, no skill trees.
- Enchantment system replaces skill trees: items have 1–3 enchantment slots, player spends enchantment points to pick one of three random options per slot.
- Salvage system: scrap old gear to recover emeralds and enchantment points — no item is pure waste.
- Artifacts: cooldown-based utility abilities (lightning rod, regeneration totem, smoke bomb, animal companion summon, etc.) — informal role specialization in co-op.
- Vendor: randomized stock refreshed on timer; no targeted crafting.
- Co-op: 4-player local or online; no public matchmaking (invite-only); revive mechanic; shared loot.
- Difficulty: Adventure + Apocalypse tiers unlocked after campaign; same levels rescaled.
- Secret levels unlocked via runes or exploration paths.
- DLC chapters (Jungle Awakens, Creeping Winter, Howling Peaks, Flames of the Nether, Hidden Depths, Echoing Void) substantially extended content.
- Criticism: flat loot excitement, no build-defining uniques, no set items, vendor as random pull = "loot boxes."
- Available on Game Pass at launch; cross-play across platforms.

## Chronicon (2020 full release, Subworld)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://store.steampowered.com/app/375480/Chronicon/
- https://www.subworldgames.com/about/
- https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2213786888

**Key facts:**
- Early Access 2015; 1.0 August 21, 2020. Developer: Subworld (Daniel Stigsjöö + Marika Assgård), near Gothenburg, Sweden. Pixel art, proprietary engine.
- Won Steam 2020 Early Access Graduate Silver Award. 94% positive, 3,307+ English reviews.
- Four classes: Templar, Berserker, Warden, Warlock. Each has 4 mixed-and-matchable skill trees.
- Over 900 skills, abilities, and perks total. Passive skill tree layer.
- Itemization: 400+ unique items (fixed special powers) + 700+ base items (randomized enchantments and qualities). Set items. Crafting layers: enchanting, gem insertion, empowering, rune inscription.
- Unique power modifier extraction: harvest a modifier from a unique/legendary/true-legendary and graft it onto preferred gear (one time only). Allows targeted build completion over pure RNG.
- Endgame: Anomalies = randomly generated dungeons, NO keys/maps required, unlimited free access.
- Mastery system: infinite ranks above level cap, each granting a Mastery Point for a secondary passive tree. Explicitly uncapped.
- Co-op: up to 4-player local/split-screen; Remote Play Together for online.
- DLCs: Ancient Beasts (Feb 2022), The Mechanist (Jan 2023 — adds 5th class with jetpack + gun/axe).
- Platforms: Windows, Mac, Linux, Steam Deck.
- Community-driven development during Early Access; many player suggestions incorporated.

## Sacred 2: Fallen Angel (2008, Ascaron Entertainment)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacred_2:_Fallen_Angel
- https://www.gamerevolution.com/review/43577-sacred-2-fallen-angel-review-3
- https://www.analogstickgaming.com/game-reviews/2025/11/21/sacred-2-fallen-angel-remaster

**Key facts:**
- Released late 2008 (PC), May 2009 (consoles). Developer: Ascaron Entertainment (Paderborn, Germany). Engine: proprietary 3D with isometric camera. Ascaron went insolvent shortly after launch.
- Remaster released late 2025.
- World: Ancaria, 22 square miles, seamless between biomes (desert, rainforest, tundra), multi-level dungeons up to 4 stories. NPCs follow day/night routines. Minimal loading transitions.
- Seven classes (fixed gender): Seraphim, Shadow Warrior, High Elf, Dryad, Temple Guardian, Inquisitor, Dragon Mage.
- Combat Arts: ability system where arts are leveled individually; modification runes alter behavior (AoE, damage type, cooldown vs. charge). Arts slot into "combos" — player-defined macros that execute arts in sequence.
- Buff stacking penalty: activating any buff-type art increases regeneration time of ALL other arts globally.
- Dual campaign paths: Light vs. Shadow, different quest objectives and conclusions.
- Mounts: class-specific, can cast Combat Arts while mounted; function as additional equipment slots.
- Level cap: at least 200.
- Itemization: randomized modifiers, class-weighted drops, sockets for runes, blacksmith forging (embed items to transfer stats). Runes are dual-use: forge into weapon OR consume to level a Combat Art.
- Co-op: hot-swap mechanic — leave solo campaign, join multiplayer, return to solo at exact point left, retaining all gains. PC: up to 16 players free-play/PvP. Console: 4 online / 2 split-screen.
- Shipped buggy; patches improved stability significantly.

## Van Helsing Final Cut (2015, NeocoreGames)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Incredible_Adventures_of_Van_Helsing
- https://neocoregames.com/en/games/the-incredible-adventures-of-van-helsing-final-cut/overview
- https://goldplatedgames.com/2017/08/11/review-the-incredible-adventures-of-van-helsing-final-cut/

**Key facts:**
- Released November 6, 2015 (PC), later console. Developer: NeocoreGames (Hungary). Engine: Helsing 3 (proprietary, improved load times + frame rate over prior engine).
- Final Cut = all three Van Helsing games unified into one campaign with six classes introduced retroactively.
- Six classes: Hunter (melee), Assassin (stealth), Sniper, Warlock, Soldier (armored), Engineer (turrets/robots).
- Each class: 24 skills, 12 auras, 3 unique abilities. Rage resource (third bar alongside HP/mana) powers per-skill bonus unlocks — spending Rage on a skill triggers a power state for that skill specifically.
- Katarina companion: AI-controlled ghost. Has own inventory, own skill trees (combat tree + Sentinel passive tree). Mode-switched by player: melee mode / ranged mode / Ghostly Form (invisible, invulnerable, passive bonuses only, cannot attack).
- Katarina levels alongside player but slightly slower.
- Tower defense segments: optional at story points, player places defensive structures while fighting alongside them. Reviewed as "surprisingly fun" by multiple sources.
- Itemization: high loot volume but limited affix complexity; dominant upgrade strategy = highest power wins.
- Endgame: Scenario Mode with standalone missions and challenge layers.
- Co-op: up to 4 players online.
- Controller support praised as best-in-class for the genre with radial menus and redesigned UI.
- NeocoreGames later made Warhammer Inquisitor Martyr using similar ARPG expertise.

## Warhammer 40,000: Inquisitor — Martyr (2018, NeocoreGames)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warhammer_40,000:_Inquisitor_%E2%80%93_Martyr
- https://thirdcoastreview.com/games-tech/2018/06/11/game-review-inquisitor-martyr
- https://neocoregames.com/en/games/warhammer-40k-inquisitor-martyr
- https://neocoregames.com/en/community/hub/announcing-inquisitor-martyr-seasonal-journey

**Key facts:**
- Released June 5, 2018 (PC), August 23, 2018 (PS4/Xbox One). Developer and publisher: NeocoreGames (Hungary). Engine: Unreal Engine 4. Next-gen upgrade 2022.
- Setting: Caligari Sector, a fictional Warhammer 40K galaxy created specifically for this game.
- Four classes: Crusader (armored, melee/ranged), Psyker (warp powers, AoE/debuffs), Assassin (stealth, fast/light armor), Tech-Adept (Prophecy DLC 2019, robotic minions).
- Each class has 3 subclasses. Armor type equipped changes available skills.
- Combat: slower than Diablo-peers, deliberate pacing to match Warhammer atmosphere. Destructible environments.
- Cover system: environmental cover for damage reduction. Weakness: enemies use it very effectively; player cover is often destroyed before use. Remained a consistent criticism even post-patch.
- Itemization: power-level system gates story mission access → forces grinding procedurally generated side missions. Item comparison largely overridden by power number.
- Persistent galaxy: Caligari Sector as shared online world. Hundreds of star systems / thousands of planets. Procedurally generated mission maps. Global events permanently alter galaxy state.
- Seasons: originally sequential; 2.0 overhaul made 7 concurrent seasons simultaneously available at character creation. Players pick a season at start; each has unique progression tracks and cosmetic rewards.
- Offline mode: launched as online-only; offline mode added 2024 under player pressure.
- Co-op: 4-player online. PvP: 1v1 and 2v2 arena.
- Metacritic: 65–71 across platforms.
- 2.0 patch was major redesign pushing toward more traditional ARPG feel.
- Significant post-launch DLC and free updates despite main studio moving to other projects (maintained by endgame-focused sub-team).

## Loot River (2022, straka.studio)

**Sources fetched:**
- https://lootriver.com/press/sheet.php?p=loot_river
- https://www.escapistmagazine.com/loot-river-review-in-3-minutes-block-shifting-mechanics-meet-roguelike-action/
- https://80.lv/articles/loot-river-a-game-about-unforgiving-procedural-labyrinths
- https://eip.gg/reviews/loot-river-is-an-innovative-but-flawed-roguelike/
- https://gameinformer.com/review/loot-river/pieces-sailing-into-place

**Key facts:**
- Released May 3, 2022 (PC/Xbox), December 19, 2023 (PS4/PS5). Developer: straka.studio (Slovakia). Backed by SUPERHOT PRESENTS + Slovak Arts Council.
- Engine: not publicly disclosed. Visual style: hand-drawn pixel art with real-time 3D shadows and water simulation.
- Core mechanic: right-stick (or equivalent) slides the platform the player stands on across water, subject to available space. Platforms are Tetris-shaped sections of procedurally arranged floating dungeon ruins.
- Tile-shifting serves three functions: (1) navigation puzzle — connect platforms to explore; (2) combat tactic — isolate enemies by disconnecting platforms; (3) encounter skipping — flee and disconnect.
- Most enemies cannot cross water gaps, making disconnection a high-skill defensive option.
- Combat: Dark Souls-inspired. Normal attack, charged attack, roll/dodge, parry (timing-based, brief invulnerability + devastating counter). Various weapon types (swords, axes, staves) with different movesets and stat scaling.
- Loot: run-scoped (temporary). Permanent progression via "unholy knowledge" extractions across runs.
- Roguelite loop: procedurally generated labyrinths, multiple boss floors gating depth, permanent upgrades unlocked over successive runs.
- Post-launch: level editor added for custom platform layouts + community sharing.
- Inspirations: Dark Souls (combat difficulty) + Tetris (spatial manipulation).
- Reception: mixed — praised for originality of mechanic, criticized for shallow build depth and difficulty spikes.
